questions.stem: An instrument used to measure the amount of water vapor in the air is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The instrument that measures the amount of water vapour or humidity in the atmosphere is called Hygrometer. The measurement is expressed in percentage.'
A barometer measures air pressure, a thermometer temperature, a rain gauge rainfall and a wind vane wind direction. Answer: A.
tips: Match each weather element with its instrument: humidity – hygrometer; pressure – barometer; wind speed – anemometer; wind direction – wind vane; rainfall – rain gauge.

similar_questions.stem: The instrument used to measure the speed of the wind is the
explanation_steps: An anemometer measures wind speed; a wind vane shows only its direction.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: All are members of the inner planets in the solar system, <u>except</u>
explanation_steps: The textbook: the planets 'form two groups: terrestrial or inner planets and outer or giant planets. The inner planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.'
Jupiter is the largest of the outer (giant) planets. Answer: E.
tips: Inner (rocky) planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars. Outer (giant) planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is an outer (giant) planet?
explanation_steps: Saturn lies beyond the asteroid belt and is a gas giant.
Answer: D.

textbook_ref.section: The solar system – inner and outer planets

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>would not</u> be considered as part of the study in physical geography?
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Physical geography is the study of the natural environment' (landforms, climate, soils, vegetation, water), while 'Human geography is the study of the relationships between human beings and the' environment, including their economic activities.
Soil, climate and natural vegetation are parts of the natural environment. Agriculture is a human economic activity, so it belongs to human (economic) geography. Answer: D.
tips: Ask 'did people make it or do it?' – if yes, it is human geography (agriculture, settlement, population, trade).

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is studied in human geography?
explanation_steps: Population is about people, so it is part of human geography.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: In Africa, volcanic mountains are commonly found in
explanation_steps: Volcanoes form where the crust is being pulled apart or where plates meet. In Africa the main zone of crustal stretching is the East African Rift System.
The textbook names Mt. Kenya and Mt. Elgon as extinct volcanoes; Kilimanjaro (Tanzania) is also a volcano, and the Afar region of Eritrea and Ethiopia has active ones (Dubbi, Alid, Erta Ale).
So volcanic mountains are most common in Eastern Africa. Answer: B.
tips: East Africa = rift valleys + volcanoes (Kilimanjaro, Kenya, Elgon, Meru). North-west Africa = fold mountains (Atlas). South Africa = old plateaus and residual/block mountains (Drakensberg).

similar_questions.stem: The Atlas Mountains of north-west Africa are an example of
explanation_steps: The Atlas were formed by folding when the African plate pushed against the Eurasian plate.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries <u>is not</u> categorized as one of the least developed countries?
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'In the least developed countries like Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, Eritrea and Chad, more than 75% of the population is engaged in agriculture. In contrast … the advanced countries like Canada, France, the USA, Sweden …'
Canada is a rich, highly industrialised (developed) country; the other four are African developing countries. Answer: E.
tips: The textbook uses 'least developed' loosely for poor African countries. On the official UN list of Least Developed Countries, Ethiopia and Zambia are LDCs but Kenya and Nigeria are not – yet Canada is still the only clearly developed country here.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a developed (advanced) country?
explanation_steps: Sweden is an industrialised, high-income country.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.section: 4.2 Economic measures of development – employment structure

questions.stem: Which of the following places in Eritrea has two rainy seasons?
explanation_steps: The textbook on the Eastern Escarpment (700–2000 m): 'The region gets rainfall both from north-east trade winds and south-westerly winds. It has two rainy seasons.'
Filfil (Filfil–Solomuna, the 'Green Belt') lies on the Eastern Escarpment, so it gets summer rain from the south-westerlies and winter rain from the north-east winds.
Asmara and Mendefera (central highlands) and Nakfa (northern highlands) have one main summer rainy season; Foro on the coastal plain gets mainly winter rain. Answer: C.
tips: Eritrea's rainfall seasons: highlands and western lowlands – summer (June–September); coastal plains – winter (October–March); Eastern Escarpment (Green Belt) – both.

similar_questions.stem: The coastal plains of Eritrea receive most of their rainfall during

options.B: winter, from the north-east trade winds

explanation_steps: The coast gets its rain from the north-east winds that cross the Red Sea in winter.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors <u>is not</u> a requirement for development?
explanation_steps: The textbook (4.1.2 Requirements for Development) lists natural and human resources, 'Capital is another prerequisite for development', 'Education is the major driving force for development' and 'Peace and stability is another critical requirement for development.'
All four listed factors are requirements, so none of them is excluded. Answer: E.
tips: When every option is supported by the textbook, 'None of the above' is the answer to a 'which is not' question.

similar_questions.stem: According to the textbook, the 'major driving force for development' is
explanation_steps: The book says education is the major driving force, because development depends on the quality of people.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: An important characteristic of soil that determines its permeability is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Soil texture refers to the size of soil particles … Texture is an important factor that determines porosity and permeability of soil.'
Sandy (coarse) soils let water pass quickly; clay (fine) soils are almost impermeable. Colour, acidity and fertility do not control how fast water moves through. Answer: D.
tips: Permeability = how easily water moves through soil; porosity = how much space there is between particles. Both depend on texture.

similar_questions.stem: A soil made mostly of very fine particles (less than 0.02 mm) is
explanation_steps: The textbook: clay particles are less than 0.02 mm.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: A type of rainfall formed when warm air and cold air converge is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Frontal rainfall occurs when two winds with different temperatures meet'; the warm air rises over the cooler air mass, cools and gives 'Cyclonic or frontal rainfall.'
Orographic (= relief) rain forms when air is forced up a mountain; convectional rain forms when heated air rises. Answer: C.
tips: Three types of rain: convectional (heating), relief/orographic (mountain barrier), frontal/cyclonic (warm and cold air masses meet).

similar_questions.stem: Rainfall caused when moist wind is forced to rise over a mountain barrier is called
explanation_steps: Mountains force the air to rise, cool and condense on the windward side.
Answer: D.

questions.review_flag: Option A is printed 'Conventional' – a misprint for 'Convectional'. Key unaffected.

questions.stem: One of the following areas in Eritrea is known for its cotton cultivation.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Cotton grows in the Lowlands of Eritrea. Ali Ghider is the largest cotton growing area using water from the Gash river. The textile factories of Eritrea depend on this plantation.'
Alighider lies near Tesseney in the western lowlands. Answer: E.
tips: Link each place with its crop: Alighider – cotton (Gash river); Nefasit – sisal; western lowlands – sesame and sorghum.

similar_questions.stem: The river that supplies irrigation water to the Alighider cotton farm is the
explanation_steps: The textbook says Ali Ghider uses water from the Gash river.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following continents has the highest rate of population growth?
explanation_steps: The textbook notes that world growth has slowed since the 1960s, 'but growth remains high in the Middle East and sub Saharan Africa.'
Africa has the highest birth rates and the fastest population growth rate of any continent (about 2.5% a year); Europe's population is almost static. Answer: A.
tips: Careful: Asia has the LARGEST population, Africa the FASTEST growth rate.

similar_questions.stem: The continent with the slowest (almost zero) population growth rate is
explanation_steps: Europe has low birth rates and an ageing population.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Identify the <u>correct</u> method for prevention of soil degradation.
explanation_steps: The textbook lists soil conservation methods: terracing, contour ploughing, crop rotation and the use of fertilizers, planting trees and shelter belts, and leaving land fallow to recover fertility.
All four listed methods prevent soil degradation. Answer: E.
tips: Methods that keep soil in place (contour ploughing, terraces, trees) and methods that keep it fertile (rotation, fallowing, manure) both prevent degradation.

similar_questions.stem: Ploughing across a slope rather than up and down it is called
explanation_steps: Contour ploughing follows the contour lines so that furrows hold back running water.
Answer: B.

additional_textbook_refs.section: 5.2 Soil degradation and conservation in Eritrea

questions.stem: The Sahara Desert is a sparsely populated region mainly due to the effect of
explanation_steps: The textbook: dry climates 'encourage sparse population distributions. The Sahara desert and the Sahelian belt in Africa are good examples of sparsely populated areas due to low rainfall amounts and its irregularity.'
Low, unreliable rainfall and very high temperatures are features of climate. Answer: C.
tips: Physical factors of population distribution: climate (most important), relief, soil, water, vegetation.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following regions is densely populated mainly because of a favourable climate and fertile soils?
explanation_steps: The Nile valley has fertile alluvium and reliable water.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.section: 3.3 Distribution and density of world population

questions.stem: Which of the following economic activities creates <u>least</u> damage to the environment?
explanation_steps: Hunter-gatherers take wild food in small numbers, move on, and use simple tools; they do not clear forests, dig pits or release factory waste.
Mining (pits, waste), farming (clearing, soil erosion), lumbering (deforestation) and manufacturing (pollution) change the environment much more. Answer: C.
tips: Human impact on the environment grows with technology: hunting and gathering → farming → industry.

similar_questions.stem: Which activity is the main direct cause of deforestation?
explanation_steps: Lumbering is the cutting of trees for timber.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The most important factor in the process of soil formation is
explanation_steps: The textbook lists five soil-forming factors (parent material, climate, topography, organisms, time) and says of climate: 'This is the single most influential factor in the soil-forming process.' Its exercise repeats: 'Climate is the most important factor in soil-forming process.'
Temperature and rainfall control the speed of weathering and leaching. Answer: B.
tips: Parent material decides WHAT the soil is made of, but climate decides HOW FAST and what kind of soil forms – follow the textbook: climate.

similar_questions.stem: All soils are derived from solid bedrock called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'All soils are derived from solid bed rock called parent material.'
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Colorado Desert is found in
explanation_steps: The textbook lists the hot deserts: '… d) Mohave, Colorado and Mexican Deserts in Central and North America e) Atacama …'
The Colorado Desert lies in south-eastern California (USA) and north-west Mexico. Answer: C.
tips: Hot deserts: Sahara, Kalahari, Namib (Africa); Arabian, Thar (Asia); Mohave, Colorado, Sonoran (North America); Atacama (South America); Great Australian Desert.

similar_questions.stem: The Atacama Desert is found in
explanation_steps: The Atacama lies along the coast of northern Chile.
Answer: D.

questions.stem: All of the following crops belong to oil seeds, <u>except</u>
explanation_steps: Oil seeds are crops grown for the oil in their seeds: sesame (Eritrea's main lowland oil seed), groundnuts, flax (linseed), sunflower, niger seed.
Lentils are pulses (legumes) grown for protein, not oil. Answer: D.
tips: Pulses: lentils, chickpeas, beans, peas. Oil seeds: sesame, groundnut, flax/linseed, sunflower, niger seed.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a pulse crop?
explanation_steps: Chickpea is a legume grown for its protein-rich seeds.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The type of rock that is formed as the lava cools and crystallizes is
explanation_steps: Igneous rocks form when molten material cools. Lava is magma that has reached the surface, so rock formed from lava is extrusive (volcanic) igneous rock, e.g. basalt.
Granite is intrusive igneous rock: it cools slowly from magma deep underground, not from lava. So option E is wrong. Answer: C.
tips: Magma below ground → intrusive (granite, diorite, coarse crystals). Lava at the surface → extrusive (basalt, trachyte, fine crystals).

similar_questions.stem: Which rock is an example of intrusive igneous rock?
explanation_steps: Granite cools slowly beneath the surface and has large crystals.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following resources is renewable?
explanation_steps: Renewable (flow) resources are replaced naturally and are not used up: sunlight, wind, water, and (if managed) forests and soil.
Copper, gold, diamond and natural gas are minerals and fossil fuels formed over millions of years; once used they are gone. Answer: D.
tips: Non-renewable = minerals and fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas). Renewable = sun, wind, water, living things.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-renewable resource?
explanation_steps: Coal is a fossil fuel that cannot be replaced within human time.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: A stream extends its length through
explanation_steps: The textbook (upper course): 'Head-ward erosion is when the river erodes backward from the source. Vertical erosion is when the bed of the river is eroded.'
By eating backward into the land at its source, the stream becomes longer. Vertical (downward) erosion deepens the valley and lateral erosion widens it. Answer: D.
tips: Headward → longer; vertical/downward → deeper; lateral → wider.

similar_questions.stem: The type of river erosion that widens a valley in the middle course is
explanation_steps: Lateral erosion attacks the banks and widens the valley.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: More than half of the world's population lives in
explanation_steps: Asia has about 4.7 billion of the world's 8 billion people (about 60%), including China and India, the two most populous countries.
The textbook notes that 'many countries of Asia have their population density even reaching 4000 persons per square kilometer.' Answer: B.
tips: Asia ≈ 60% of world population; Africa ≈ 18%; Europe ≈ 9%; the Americas ≈ 13%.

similar_questions.stem: The two most populous countries in the world are
explanation_steps: China and India each have over 1.4 billion people.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, the largest exposure of sandstone is found in the
explanation_steps: The textbook (Mesozoic Era): 'Hand outcrops of sandstone are commonly found in the plateaus encircling the upper portion of the Comayli and Hadas valleys such as the Cohaito, Emba Soira, Halay and Dege-a plateaus; around Adi Keih and Senafe …'
Grade 11 describes the Eastern Highlands: 'in the south sandstone terrain is more common', with rock paintings in the sandstone caves.
Qohaito, Emba Soira, Halay, Adi Keih and Senafe are all in the Eastern Highlands. Answer: C.
tips: Eritrea's rocks: Precambrian metamorphics and granites cover about 60% of the country; Mesozoic sandstone – Eastern Highlands (Qohaito–Senafe); limestone – Denkalia; basalt – south of Asmara to Adi Quala.

similar_questions.stem: In Eritrea, outcrops of Mesozoic limestone are limited to
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Outcrops of such limestone are limited to Denkalia only.'
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The type of erosion caused by the removal of soil by rainwater through forming shallow channels is called
explanation_steps: The textbook lists sheet, splash, rill, gully and wind erosion; running water that 'flows in a tiny and narrow channel' forms a rill – 'a small channel cut in soil. It is shallow.'
Sheet erosion removes a thin even layer (no channels); splash erosion is caused by raindrops striking the ground; gullies are deep channels. Answer: E.
tips: Sheet (no channels) → rill (shallow channels) → gully (deep channels): the order of increasing severity.

similar_questions.stem: Deep channels cut into the land by running water that cannot be removed by ordinary ploughing are
explanation_steps: Gullies are deep, widened rills.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Stream meanders are

options.C: most numerous near the source of the stream.
options.D: most numerous in the stream's lower sector.

explanation_steps: Meanders are loops formed where a river flows over a gentle slope and swings from side to side, eroding the outer bank (lateral erosion) and depositing on the inner bank.

The textbook describes meanders in the middle stage, and in the lower stage, where the gradient is gentlest, the features are 'flood-plains, meanders, levees'. They are most numerous in the lower course.
Vertical erosion and down-cutting make V-shaped valleys and gorges near the source, not meanders. Answer: D.
tips: Upper course: V-valleys, waterfalls (vertical erosion). Middle/lower course: meanders, ox-bow lakes, flood plains, levees (lateral erosion and deposition).

similar_questions.stem: A meander that is cut off from the main river forms a (an)
explanation_steps: When the neck of a meander is cut through, the abandoned loop becomes an ox-bow lake.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following rock types are more susceptible to the solvent action of water?
explanation_steps: Limestone is calcium carbonate, which dissolves in rainwater containing carbon dioxide (weak carbonic acid). The textbook: 'On limestone coasts, the solvent action of sea water on calcium carbonate sets up chemical' weathering.
Basalt and granite are hard igneous rocks that resist solution; sand particles (quartz) hardly dissolve. So E is wrong. Answer: B.
tips: Solution (solvent action) = chemical weathering/erosion of soluble rocks: limestone and chalk. It forms caves and gorges in limestone areas.

similar_questions.stem: Caves and underground streams are most common in areas of
explanation_steps: Water dissolves limestone along its joints, forming caves.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The transformation of people from rural settlements to urban settlements is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Urbanization is a process through which more and more people come to live in' towns and cities, mostly through rural-to-urban migration.

A conurbation is towns grown together into one built-up area; a megalopolis is a chain of huge cities; urbanism is the urban way of life; urban sprawl is the spreading of a city into the countryside. Answer: A.
tips: Urbanization = a process (people moving to towns). Urbanism = a way of life. Conurbation/megalopolis = forms of big urban areas.

similar_questions.stem: Several towns that have grown until they join into one continuous built-up area form a
explanation_steps: That is the definition of a conurbation.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The climatic zones where Adi Keih and Massawa can be placed are ________ and ________, respectively.
explanation_steps: The textbook's vertical climate zones of Eritrea: the tropical zone is 'limited only to those places which are found below 700 meters above mean sea level … places along the Red Sea coast'; 'Places above 2000 meters are classified as cool temperate climates. The Eastern Highlands mostly have this type'; sub-tropical is 700–2000 m.
Adi Keih is at 2,423 m (Table 3.2) → temperate. Massawa is at 8 m (Table 3.1) → tropical. Answer: D.
tips: Eritrea by altitude: below 700 m tropical (hot); 700–2000 m sub-tropical; above 2000 m temperate.

similar_questions.stem: Ghinda, at 962 m on the Eastern Escarpment, belongs to the
explanation_steps: 962 m lies between 700 and 2000 m.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Mountain Ruwenzori in East Africa is an example of a
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The East African Rift valley and the Red Sea rift are examples of rift valleys, while mount Ruwenzori in East Africa is an example of block mountains.'
A block mountain (horst) is raised between faults. Unlike nearby Kilimanjaro, Ruwenzori is not a volcano. Answer: A.
tips: Block mountains: Ruwenzori (East Africa), Mount Ghedem and the Afar Alps (Eritrea), Vosges and Black Forest (Europe).

similar_questions.stem: In Eritrea, Mount Ghedem near Massawa is an example of a
explanation_steps: The textbook: the Afar Alps and Mount Gedem were uplifted and formed horsts or block mountains.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: All of the following belong to the industrialized parts of the world, <u>except</u>
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The industrialized parts of the world like North America, western Europe and East Asia …'
South Asia (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh …) is still mainly agricultural and developing. Answer: D.
tips: Major industrial regions: north-eastern USA/Great Lakes, Western Europe, East Asia (Japan, South Korea, China).

similar_questions.stem: Which country is in the industrialized region of East Asia?
explanation_steps: Japan is one of the world's leading industrial countries.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The rays of the sun are vertical over the equator on
explanation_steps: At the equinoxes the overhead (vertical) sun is at the equator and day and night are equal everywhere. The textbook uses March 21 and September 23 as the dates when the overhead sun crosses into and out of the northern hemisphere.
June 21 and December 21 are the solstices, when the sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn. Answer: B.
tips: Equinoxes: 21 March, 23 September (sun over the equator). Solstices: 21 June (Tropic of Cancer), 22 December (Tropic of Capricorn).

similar_questions.stem: On June 21 the rays of the sun are vertical over the
explanation_steps: 21 June is the northern summer solstice.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following features <u>is not</u> produced by a tectonic process?

options.B: The straight course of the Anseba River

explanation_steps: Eastern Escarpment: 'Bordering the Rift Valley are the escarpments which were formed along the main fault lines' – faulting.
Mount Ghedem: 'the Afar Alps and Mount Gedem were uplifted and formed horsts or Block Mountains' – faulting.

Straight river courses: the textbook links straight courses of Eritrean rivers to faulting ('All have straight courses associated with faulting'); the Anseba 'flows along a straight course towards Keren'.
Granitic landscapes (upper Anseba, Keren) are old Precambrian granite masses exposed and shaped by long weathering and erosion, i.e. by gradation, not by earth movements. Answer: D.
tips: Tectonic = internal earth movements (faulting, folding, uplift, volcanism). Weathering and erosion are external processes.

similar_questions.stem: The escarpments bordering the Red Sea rift in Eritrea were formed mainly by
explanation_steps: The textbook: the escarpments were formed along the main fault lines.
Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Granite itself formed from intruded magma (an internal process), so a student could argue that granitic landscapes are also 'tectonic'. Keyed D because the landscape is produced by exposure and weathering; the other three are faulting features. Teacher check.

questions.stem: The inorganic matter of soil is derived from
explanation_steps: The textbook: soil 'is an unconsolidated combination of organic and inorganic materials'; the organic part comes from decayed plants and animals (humus), while the mineral (inorganic) particles come from the weathering of the parent rock.
Air and water fill the pore spaces but are separate components. Answer: D.
tips: Four components of soil: inorganic (mineral) matter from rocks ≈ 45%, organic matter (humus), air and water.

similar_questions.stem: The dark organic matter in soil formed from decayed plants and animals is called
explanation_steps: Humus is decomposed organic matter.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Modern transportation system in Eritrea began during the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Modern transport began in Eritrea during the Italian colonial period.' The Massawa–Asmara railway was built 1887–1911, and 'The existing road network of Eritrea was built during the Italian period between 1934 and 1939.'
Answer: B.
tips: Italian legacy in transport: the Massawa–Asmara–Keren–Agordat railway, the Asmara–Massawa cable way and the main road network.

similar_questions.stem: Most of Eritrea's existing main road network was built between
explanation_steps: The textbook dates the road network to 1934–1939, when Italy prepared to invade Ethiopia.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the following places in Eritrea is known for its potash deposits.
explanation_steps: The textbook: when the inland Danakil sea dried up it left 'deposits of potash, gypsum, salt and other lacustrine materials behind. The Bada plain is living evidence of this process.'
Colluli (Caluli) in the Bada/Danakil area is Eritrea's potash project. Bisha is a copper–zinc–gold mine; Zara and Dubarwa are gold areas. Answer: C.
tips: Eritrea's minerals: Bisha (gold, copper, zinc), Zara and Koka (gold), Asmara/Debarwa (copper, gold), Colluli (potash), Massawa and Assab (salt).

similar_questions.stem: The Bisha mine in western Eritrea mainly produces
explanation_steps: Bisha is a polymetallic mine (gold, copper, zinc).
Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: The textbook names the Bada plain and potash deposits but not 'Colluli/Caluli' itself (the potash mining project dates from after the textbook). Key unaffected.

questions.stem: A widely used measure of economic development is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Per capita income is a widely used economic measure of development. It is the' total national income divided by the population.

Energy consumption and employment structure are other economic measures, and literacy and nourishment are social measures, but per capita income is the one the textbook calls 'widely used'. Answer: E.
tips: Per capita income = national income ÷ population. Composite measure: Human Development Index (income + education + health).

similar_questions.stem: A country's national income is 6 billion Nakfa and its population is 3 million. Its per capita income is
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following items is an example of primary source of history?
explanation_steps: Primary sources were produced at the time of the event by people who took part in or saw it: 'Primary sources include letters, diaries, tax rolls, treaties, tools, clothing, art' and eyewitness accounts.
Books, articles and theses written later by historians who studied the event are secondary sources. Answer: B.
tips: Primary = first-hand, from the time (eyewitness, diary, artefact, treaty). Secondary = later interpretation (textbook, article, thesis).

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a secondary source of history?
explanation_steps: A textbook is written later from other sources.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>was not</u> among the inventions of the ancient Chinese civilization?
explanation_steps: Paper, printing, gunpowder and the magnetic compass are the 'four great inventions' of China. The textbook: 'Gunpowder was also invented during the Tang dynasty', and the Sui, Tang and Song dynasties are credited with the 'inventions of printing and gunpowder'.
